sections.heading: Why a Visit Before Each Season
body: Furnaces and air conditioners fail at the worst times because the small problems are quiet. A dirty filter, a plugged drain or dust caked on a coil won't announce themselves in April. Instead they surface on the first hot afternoon or the first cold night.
A check before heating season and another before cooling season finds those problems on a calm day, with the answers to your questions in the same visit.

sections.heading: Small Problems That Don't Announce Themselves
body: Most breakdowns start as something small and easy to miss. Here is what we mean.

items.title: A clogged air filter
items.text: Air has to move through the system. A clogged filter makes the blower work harder and can leave rooms uncomfortable long before anything fails.

items.title: A plugged condensate drain
items.text: An air conditioner pulls water out of the air. When the drain backs up, that water has nowhere to go.

items.title: Dust on the coil
items.text: A dirty coil makes an air conditioner run longer to do less.

items.title: A worn part nobody has looked at
items.text: Parts wear out slowly, and a technician who is looking at the whole system sees them before they quit.

sections.heading: What a Visit Looks Like
body: A maintenance visit is an inspection and a cleaning. The technician looks over the equipment, cleans what needs cleaning and answers your questions.
Ask what you want to know. How old is the system? Is that noise normal? Should you plan to replace anything in a few years?
By the time the technician leaves, you should know what was checked, what was cleaned and what to keep an eye on before the next visit. If any of that is unclear, ask before the truck pulls away.

image.alt: Ceiling air vent in a quiet room

sections.heading: Heating in the Fall, Cooling in the Spring
body: The two visits have different jobs. Each one gets the system ready for the season ahead.

items.title: Before the heating season
items.text: The furnace gets its look in the fall, while the weather is still mild. If something is worn, you find out when you can still wait a few days for a part.

items.title: Before the cooling season
items.text: The air conditioner gets its look in the spring. A plugged drain or a dirty coil is easier to deal with in May than in July.

items.title: In between
items.text: If something acts up between visits, you already know who to call, and the technician has seen the system recently.

sections.heading: Who Belongs on the Schedule
body: Anyone with a furnace or an air conditioner can sign up, and a few situations make it especially worth doing. A system that's getting older is one. A brand-new system is another, because it should start clean and stay that way.
Landlords belong on the list too, because a tenant's no-cool call lands on you. So do owners of a second property, who can't check on the equipment themselves. Tell the office about each address.
